# A pending container approval follows a retargeted host to another machine

Reviewed commit: 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435

## TLDR

A user can approve an agent's card naming one container host and have Farhelm create the container, run its command and deliver the recipe's credentials on a different machine. Changing the host's SSH destination while the card waits does not invalidate it; the launch uses the changed destination after a fresh Podman check.

## Details

The route is a first container launch at an ordinary SSH place that has a usable Podman probe but no existing environment rows or recipe images/helpers. An ordinary agent issues create --recipe <recipe> --container-host <host>. plan_environment_create resolves the name into Place::PodmanHost(id) (agent_requests.rs:4180-4209). launch_environment_for_agent reads the display name before approval (4485-4491), then freezes that old name and numeric place in ApprovalAction::LaunchEnvironment (4493-4515), with the resolved command and launch fixed. No destination, entry UUID, connection or BaseRoute snapshot for the container PLACE is retained. The card can remain pending while the operator changes that SSH row's destination in Hosts. hosts.rs:1121-1165 calls store.update_ssh_destination; store.rs:7521-7599 permits an ordinary SSH retarget after store/podman.rs:215-253 verifies no environment/resource references. Pending cards are not among those references, and the agent has not registered an environment yet. A recipe with no images at this place is valid because Podman builds lazily: RecipeState::require_launch_source does nothing for Podman (environment/recipes.rs:259-268).

After refreshing that row's Podman probe for the new endpoint (hosts.rs:1669; podman_probe.rs:435-477), Allow still succeeds: approvals.rs:435-570 tracks only the requesting session/connection, and approved at agent_requests.rs:2865-2893 rechecks only that origin. The only extra target recheck here is for a clone source (4519-4528), absent on create. The handler passes the same numeric place to start_session_environment at 4541-4550. That task validates CURRENT provider availability and registers the row (provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:346-400), then ensure_prepared and all commands resolve the place's CURRENT endpoint (environment/podman.rs:148-188,950-1033). They compare against the current probe, not the route the card named. A refreshed success for machine B therefore admits launch on B while the card still names A. Source-side environment ownership/admission guards do not compare A and B because this launch has no prior resource.

The credential consequence is present in shipped code, not hypothetical additional functionality: environment_session_steps calls delivery.setup with this recipe at provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:597-605. credential_delivery.rs:347-368 applies the recipe, resolves the new environment's current access route at 434-440, and installs a configured Codex login at 575-609 or recipe GitHub token at 614-654. Those secrets are now inside a container on B. The operator's separate retarget action does not answer or redraw the pending agent confirmation that still names A.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md:9548-9556 says ‘What a card shows is what an approval does’ and ‘A launch is also refused if the target host's connection changed while the card waited, since the approval was for the machine the card named.’ SPEC.md:4330-4332 specifically requires the environment card to name where the environment will be created. SPEC_impl.md:1071-1074 requires answered controls to act on what was drawn. The recipe/place encoding being separate from an installed-host identity (6506-6509) specifies reusable placement, not permission for a confirmation to silently follow a changed physical endpoint. Keep the place route/entry snapshot with the planned launch and reject a mismatch after Allow under admission that cannot race the destination writer; alternatively invalidate the old card and ask for the new target.

Suggested bucket: highest — the established route delivers configured recipe credentials and execution to a machine the pending approval did not name. Confidence: confirmed by source and contract analysis; no runtime execution or reproduction. Caveats: requires a concurrent operator retarget plus a successful fresh probe before Allow, and a place with no existing environments or retained images/helpers (the reference guard otherwise blocks retargeting). No malicious-agent host-edit capability is required. Reconnection alone without an endpoint change is not the credential-exposure route asserted here. The earlier recipe-definition concern remains dropped: this finding is specifically changed container-host authority, and does not allege that selecting a recipe name freezes all future recipe edits. Could-be-highest: yes, with the shipped credential path above established. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none.

# Sandbox agent launches ask for approval before checking the local SSH key

Reviewed commit: 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435

## TLDR

When Farhelm's local Tensorlake SSH key is missing or unreadable, an agent can still raise an Allow/Deny card for a new sandbox. Allow can only fail with a prerequisite that was already knowable before asking, although the GUI disables the same launch. The user must answer an unnecessary approval before receiving the actionable setup error.

## Details

In crates/farhelm-helm/src/agent_requests.rs:4390-4507, launch_environment_for_agent performs its pre-card checks through provider.places(), RecipeState::require_launch_source and CreateReq::validate_sandbox_launch. None checks the local SSH key: Tensorlake's places implementation at crates/farhelm-helm/src/tensorlake/hosts.rs:187-192 checks only the API key; RecipeState::require_launch_source at environment/recipes.rs:259-268 checks only snapshot presence; sessions.rs:1258-1333 validates destination, launch and prompt. Given an API key and built recipe, the request therefore reaches approved at agent_requests.rs:4480 even with SshKeyStatus::NotCreated or Unavailable. The first local-key prerequisite is hosts.rs:205-219 in ensure_prepared, after the approved request starts the owned launch task and registers the environment row (provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:346-400, 525-554). That check deterministically refuses a non-Ready key before any billed preparation/create. Tensorlake::settings reads the absent/unreadable states separately at tensorlake/mod.rs:298-315, so snapshot presence does not certify key readiness.

The explicit contract is SPEC_impl.md:6683-6685: ‘Before asking, the helm checks the place's cached availability and the launcher's own environment-launch validation, so the user is never asked to approve a launch that is then refused before anything starts.’ SPEC.md:1451-1453 also disables sandbox selection for an absent or unreadable local Farhelm SSH key. This is a promised specific prerequisite guard, rather than a demand to discover whether Tensorlake has registered the public key (the latter is explicitly not checkable). Apply the provider's existing local-key admission before raising the agent card, retaining its post-Allow recheck for changes during the wait.

Suggested bucket: other — an unnecessary approval and delayed prerequisite refusal, with no established billing, data-loss or security consequence. Confidence: confirmed by source and contract analysis; no runtime behavior observed and no reproduction written. Caveat: requires a built recipe and a missing/unreadable local key (for example after state recovery loses the separate key files); it does not affect normally configured keys, nor does it start paid work because the provider's later guard prevents that. Could-be-highest: no. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none.

# Agent environment launches enter GUI convenience bookkeeping

Reviewed commit: 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435

## TLDR

A successful environment launch requested by an agent can change the container host preselected in the GUI and push the user's own recent setups out of its history. The new agent environment route carries enough trusted target data to update history, but being a valid target does not make it a GUI choice.

## Details

This is the agent consumer of caller-supplied g050/l1 line8, independently checked here; it is not a newly claimed storage root cause. The assigned new path at agent_requests.rs:4477-4484 creates CreateReq::for_agent_environment, and :4541-4548 dispatches it to start_session_environment. sessions.rs:1192-1253 retains its agent marker and origin() returns CreateOrigin::Agent. provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:357-361 nevertheless attaches environment_target independently; the launch task sends that same request into create_in_session_sandbox at :1007-1013. sessions.rs:1756-1802 passes it to create_session_request, whose :1848-1863 retains origin before taking the private approved launch; :1893-1894 separately captures environment_target. do_create_session_with_environment at :2055-2060 correctly withholds explicit_selection for agents, but accept_created_session/record_created_history at :2144-2242 still pass environment_target into record_create_history_with_environment_if_current. The live-claim closure explicitly admits a session-owned host when environment_target exists. There is no agent-origin input left to distinguish this target from a raw command selected in the GUI.

store.rs:8835-8890 admits the current claim and :9015-9018 calls environment_history::record with target independently from optional selection. store/environment_history.rs:49-54 accepts a target with None selection, :60-75 inserts its admission marker, :82-88 overwrites last_container_host, and :93-99 ages the same bounded window. The reader :111-114 hides None-selection rows but does not undo their eviction of structured GUI history. Current-claim and fresh-admission checks certify the successful create and prevent replay, not GUI provenance. A newly created environment with a fresh session supplies the normal successful admission.

Exact contract at SPEC.md:5158-5163: 'Only what the user explicitly selects in the GUI may affect the GUI’s future defaults and suggestions' and 'anything an agent creates do not qualify, because none of them is a choice the user made in the GUI.' The user's per-request Allow is approval of an agent-selected launch, not the GUI-launch provenance that explicit_selection continues to enforce. Preserve agent origin through convenience-bookkeeping admission or suppress these GUI effects for the agent environment consumer, while keeping GUI command launches eligible despite their None structured selection.

Suggested bucket: other (wrong future place default and eviction of convenience suggestions, no established security or loss of user-owned work). Confidence: confirmed by pinned source and contract; no execution. Could-be-highest: no established route. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: same underlying provenance issue as g050/l1 line8, parent owns deduplication; this record identifies the assigned new agent entry point's integration. Caveats: needs successful approved create on a current host connection; enough successful creates are needed to evict the whole recent window. Distinct from g020/l1 physical-host consent and g020/l3 preflight timing. Original interface consequence retained. No unresolved source premise remains for this consumer.

# Environment wait comment promises an unguaranteed relay ordering

Reviewed commit: 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435

## TLDR

The new environment-launch explanation tells maintainers that the helm's still-launching answer reaches the agent before its relay deadline. The two timers start at different phases, so that is only the normal outcome, not a guarantee. Slow work before approval or registration can consume the spare relay budget first. The existing unknown-outcome response is still correct; this finding is the misleading timing explanation.

## Details

The assigned new comment at agent_requests.rs:4550-4554 says the relay budget covers approval plus the local launch allowance, ‘so answering by the end of the allowance after the Allow reaches the agent before its relay gives up’, with the still-launching explanation ‘instead of a lost answer.’ The local timeout at :4555-4557 starts after both approved (:4493-4515) and an awaited start_session_environment registration (:4541-4549). Registration itself performs store/provider reads and an unbounded add_confirmations.lock_owned await (provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:357-390) before returning its result receiver. Pre-card planning/source discovery also precedes approved.

The relay instead composes 30 seconds ordinary answer budget plus nine-minute approval allowance plus thirty-minute environment allowance (service/agent_relay.rs:640-663; service/core.rs:312,476-478; proto/approvals.rs:24-45). HelmLink::upcall starts this one answer timer once the request is QUEUED on the connection, at agent_relay.rs:317-326, before the helm's source/planning/approval/registration phases. The approval deadline starts later when Approvals inserts the card at approvals.rs:485-538. There is no shared monotonic deadline passed to the local environment timeout and no budget subtraction for those intervening phases. If pre-card plus post-Allow pre-timeout work exceeds the ordinary 30-second spare plus unused approval allowance, the relay deadline precedes the local thirty-minute timeout. A near-end-of-window Allow and slow source/registration phases suffice for the timing inequality; no runtime incidence or exact delay is asserted.

This limitation is explicitly part of the governing contract, rather than a request to tighten timers: SPEC_impl.md:9390-9396 says the relay's extra thirty seconds is ‘an allowance for the work the helm does before and after the wait, not a guaranteed ordering’, and gives slow clone source resolution as an example. The environment-specific paragraph at :6692-6698 carefully says the agent ‘normally hears that before its relay gives up’. SPEC.md:4336-4340 and proto/approvals.rs:35-44 count approval and launch against one span and retain unknown outcome while owned work continues. The new comment omits this phase-origin caveat and makes a guarantee those contracts expressly do not make. Qualify it to normal delivery with remaining relay budget and name the different timer origins; do not claim that the local timeout itself guarantees its message wins.

The complete relevant-path diff from that commit to inclusive 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db has no later change to these timeout/comment lines. No pre-range implementation bug is attributed to this range.

Confidence: confirmed from timer starts, additive budgets, call ordering and explicit governing contract; no execution, reproduction or build. Could-be-highest: no established security or user-work-loss route; lost detailed explanation still produces the specified unknown outcome and does not cancel the task. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none in the complete refreshed interface records; supplied g123/l1 concerns a separate Delete admission/decision deadline and g026/g027 browser-gate findings concern different test waits. # Environment create replies can mark an earlier connection result current

Reviewed commit: 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435. TLDR: after a new sandbox or container successfully creates its first session, a disconnect and reconnect before its reply is projected can make the agent receive the earlier connection’s session state marked fresh under the replacement connection. The successful creation and stable session reference remain valid; the defect is false connection freshness, not a new launch on another machine.

Details: create_in_session_sandbox obtains the operation’s real (claim, session) from create_session_request, but discards the claim and returns only entry-qualified SessionInfo (sessions.rs:1756-1802). create_session_request captures claim/client together before dispatch (:1844-1868) and returns that original claim after create/bookkeeping (:1923-1925). finish_session_launch then awaits set_step and memory.lock before sending only the session through its result channel (provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:1018-1057). The agent caller receives that earlier result and obtains a NEW current claim via host_client at agent_requests.rs:4578-4588. agent_row_of_mutation :4690-4710 compares this new claim with current snapshots, so a replacement connection yields host:Some/current name and stale:false for the earlier result. The comparison cannot detect the replacement because the original incarnation was discarded.

The replacement premise is source-supported independently of operator retarget: setup releases its connection hold before attach_supervisor (tensorlake_add.rs:615-622). The resource provisioning guard excludes coordinated resource operations, not actor transport reconnection. The actor’s run/refresh loop independently exits on client.closed and redials (manager.rs:3588-3668,4720); publish mints a new incarnation whenever the client changes, including going away (:5190-5208). The result sender and agent receiver are separate tasks, with awaited bookkeeping before sending, and neither carries a connection lease through projection. Thus the earlier operation may already have completed successfully while the actor reconnects before the receiving task samples its claim. No timing frequency or runtime occurrence was measured.

Contract: AgentSession.host at proto/lib.rs:2656-2668 explicitly says every mutating reply, including the two creating verbs, pins the row to the connection the mutation actually routed through and marks lost ownership as stale with host:None. Its host_id contract :2640-2644 preserves the original claim without asserting current incarnation. The ordinary agent mutation projection’s own complete contract (agent_requests.rs:4599-4635) states the same same-connection requirement; the new environment caller bypasses it by re-minting the input claim. The new local comment :4575-4577 promises the stale fallback after loss but only handles a host still disconnected at the sampling moment. Preserve the original SessionClaim through the owned provisioning result and project against it, or explicitly emit a stale result when that claim cannot be retained; do not substitute a later connection claim for the operation’s.
